text: Give me every E. coli heat-shock expression study, with their accessions.

Abstract
The objective was to enumerate Escherichia coli heat‑shock–related expression studies in NCBI GEO and provide their Series accessions. We queried GEO Series (entry_type=gse) for Escherichia coli using four synonymous terms to capture common phrasing: “heat shock,” “heat stress,” “thermal stress,” and “heat‑shock.” Each query was executed with functions.geo_search (max_results=20). NCBI automatically rewrote the queries via MeSH (e.g., “heat-shock response”), and each call reported a total matching count but returned a trimmed subset (10 records visible per call in this response). From the visible records, we filtered to studies with experiment_type containing “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing” or “Expression profiling by array,” deduplicated by Series accession, and compiled the list with titles and FTP provenance URLs. Across the queries, the reported totals were 50 (heat shock), 57 (heat stress), 7 (thermal stress), and 50 (heat‑shock). From the 40 visible records, 10 unique Series met expression criteria: GSE7656, GSE211825, GSE283248, GSE289056, GSE305476, GSE312438, GSE269907, GSE330026, GSE272161, and GSE283264. This list provides concrete starting points for analyzing E. coli heat‑shock transcriptional responses. Due to NCBI’s rewriting and the response-size cap, the list is incomplete relative to the totals; further retrieval (by year slicing or stricter field terms) is warranted to exhaustively cover all matching Series.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli mounts a conserved heat‑shock response involving chaperones and proteases that remodel protein homeostasis and transcription following temperature upshift. Expression studies measuring genome‑wide transcription under heat stress or heat shock are foundational for understanding this response.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. A complete, provenance‑linked list of E. coli heat‑shock expression Series accessions in GEO was not assembled prior to this query.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Identify E. coli GEO Series measuring expression under heat‑shock/heat‑stress contexts and report their accessions. Hypothesis: Synonym-expanded GEO searches will return a nonzero set of expression Series matching heat‑stress conditions that can be filtered and deduplicated into an accession list.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We targeted NCBI GEO Series because it is GEO’s reuse unit for expression studies. To capture wording variation, we ran four searches using synonymous terms and filtered on experiment_type to retain expression (RNA‑seq or microarray) studies.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO via functions.geo_search.
Procedures.
- functions.geo_search arguments:
  1) organism="Escherichia coli", term="heat shock", entry_type="gse", max_results=20.
  2) organism="Escherichia coli", term="heat stress", entry_type="gse", max_results=20.
  3) organism="Escherichia coli", term="thermal stress", entry_type="gse", max_results=20.
  4) organism="Escherichia coli", term="heat-shock", entry_type="gse", max_results=20.
- For each returned record, we read accession, title, experiment_type, sample_count, and ftp_directory_url.
- Inclusion criterion: experiment_type containing “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing” or “Expression profiling by array.”
- Deduplication: unique GEO Series accession across all four searches.
Statistical Analysis.
- Per query, total_count was taken from geo_search.total_count; visible records counted as returned_in_response=10 (the server trimmed each 20-result list to 10).
- Expression filtering: counted from the ‘experiment_type’ field of each visible record.
- Deduplication: unique Series accession across the four visible 10-record subsets.
- Final compiled list count: 10 unique accessions meeting expression criteria.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. GEO query totals and visible results
| Query term     | total_count | returned_in_response |
|----------------|-------------|----------------------|
| heat shock     | 50          | 10                   |
| heat stress    | 57          | 10                   |
| thermal stress | 7           | 7                    |
| heat-shock     | 50          | 10                   |

Table 2. Retrieved E. coli heat‑shock–related expression Series (visible subset, deduplicated)
| Accession  | Title                                                                                                   | experiment_type                                       | sample_count | FTP URL                                                                                           |
|------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE7656    | E.coli GeneChip study of E.coli responses to osmotic and heat stresses                                  | Expression profiling by array                          | 18           | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE7nnn/GSE7656/                                          |
| GSE211825  | Spatial Chromosome Organization and Adaptation of Escherichia coli under Heat Stress                    | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing; Other | 22           | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE211nnn/GSE211825/                                      |
| GSE283248  | Impact of thermal treatment, pulsed electric fields, and high-pressure processing on the transcriptome… | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing     | 21           | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283248/                                      |
| GSE289056  | Thermally adapted Escherichia coli keeps transcriptomic response during temperature upshift exposure     | Expression profiling by array                          | 4            | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE289nnn/GSE289056/                                      |
| GSE305476  | Deciphering Host Stress Responses for Predictable Heterologous Gene Expression in E. coli               | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing     | 74           | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE305nnn/GSE305476/                                      |
| GSE312438  | A plant-derived antimicrobial peptide… exhibiting antibacterial… stability                              | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing     | 6            | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE312nnn/GSE312438/                                      |
| GSE269907  | Cellular function of the GndA small open reading frame-encoded polypeptide during heat shock            | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing     | 12           | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE269nnn/GSE269907/                                      |
| GSE330026  | The GndA microprotein promotes cell growth during heat shock                                            | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing     | 15           | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE330nnn/GSE330026/                                      |
| GSE272161  | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome                                       | Other; Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | 64         | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272161/                                      |
| GSE283264  | Elementary 3D organization of active and silenced E. coli genome (RNA-Seq)                              | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing     | 25           | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/                                      |

Findings.
- The GEO “heat shock” query reported 50 matching Series; “heat stress” 57; “thermal stress” 7; “heat‑shock” 50.
- Each query returned 10 visible records in this response (except thermal stress, which returned 7), due to a size cap.
- Filtering the visible records to expression profiling and deduplicating yielded 10 unique Series accessions (Table 2).

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The synonym-expanded GEO queries returned nonzero totals for E. coli heat‑shock/heat‑stress contexts. From the visible subsets, 10 unique Series were expression profiling studies. This meets the objective for a provenance‑linked list from the retrieved records but does not exhaust the full totals reported by GEO.
Context. The reported totals per term indicate many additional Series beyond the visible subset. Several retrieved records are SuperSeries or mixed experiment types that also include RNA‑seq components, consistent with heat‑stress contexts tracked alongside genome organization.
Limitations. The response was trimmed, returning 10 records per query even though max_results=20; the server reported a size cap and advised that these records are not the whole answer. NCBI’s MeSH-based query rewriting can broaden matches beyond strict “heat‑shock expression,” potentially including studies with related stress or structural assays. Paging beyond 20 and per-year slicing were not available in this call. The list therefore underrepresents the full set of GEO Series matching the criteria.
Conclusion & Future Directions. We compiled 10 E. coli heat‑shock–related expression Series accessions with their FTP provenance. To approach completeness relative to GEO’s totals, next steps include: running year-bounded geo_search queries per term to circumvent size caps; adding field-qualified terms (e.g., Title contains “heat shock”); and iterating per synonym set. On request, we can expand this list and generate a downloadable CSV/TSV of the final accession set.

References
[1] NCBI GEO esearch (heat shock): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[2] NCBI GEO esearch (heat stress): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[3] NCBI GEO esearch (thermal stress): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[4] NCBI GEO esearch (heat-shock): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[5] GEO Series GSE7656 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE7nnn/GSE7656/
[6] GEO Series GSE211825 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE211nnn/GSE211825/
[7] GEO Series GSE283248 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283248/
[8] GEO Series GSE289056 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE289nnn/GSE289056/
[9] GEO Series GSE305476 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE305nnn/GSE305476/
[10] GEO Series GSE312438 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE312nnn/GSE312438/
[11] GEO Series GSE269907 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE269nnn/GSE269907/
[12] GEO Series GSE330026 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE330nnn/GSE330026/
[13] GEO Series GSE272161 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272161/
[14] GEO Series GSE283264 FTP: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/

Acknowledgments
We thank NCBI GEO and the NCBI E‑utilities service for providing the indexed Series metadata and FTP provenance. If you would like a downloadable file of the accession list, I can generate a TSV/CSV on request.
